scenes.tts: In the mouse cortex, radial glia make neurons first, then astrocytes. Same progenitors, new output. What changes?
scenes.visual: Title card: Same Progenitor, New Order. A radial glial cell on a timeline: neurons bud off first, astrocytes later.
scenes.narration: In the mouse cortex, radial glia make neurons first, then astrocytes. Same progenitors, new output. What changes?

scenes.tts: In rodent cortex, the best-studied route to astrocytes uses cytokines. Its evidence sorts into three conditions.
scenes.visual: Three gates appear, unlit: pool, signal, competence. Label: framework for the cortical cytokine route.
scenes.narration: In rodent cortex, the best-studied route to astrocytes uses cytokines. Its evidence sorts into three conditions.

scenes.tts: First, a progenitor must still be there. Proneural genes push dividing cells to become neurons.
scenes.visual: Gate 1 lights: pool. Proneural genes push a cell toward a neuron.
scenes.narration: First, a progenitor must still be there. Proneural genes push dividing cells to become neurons.

scenes.tts: Notch turns on Hes repressors, which hold proneural genes down, so the cell stays a progenitor.
scenes.visual: Notch arrow to Hes; Hes blocks proneural genes; the cell stays a progenitor.
scenes.narration: Notch turns on Hes repressors, which hold proneural genes down, so the cell stays a progenitor.

scenes.tts: Notch does not make astrocytes by itself. It keeps a reserve of progenitors for later.
scenes.visual: A reserve of progenitors stays in the wall while neurons leave.
scenes.narration: Notch does not make astrocytes by itself. It keeps a reserve of progenitors for later.

scenes.tts: Second, the signal must arrive. It is a family of cytokines: C N T F, L I F and cardiotrophin one.
scenes.caption: Second, the signal must arrive. It is a family of cytokines: CNTF, LIF and cardiotrophin-1.
scenes.visual: Gate 2 lights: signal. Three cytokines labeled CNTF, LIF, cardiotrophin-1.
scenes.narration: Second, the signal must arrive. It is a family of cytokines: CNTF, LIF and cardiotrophin-1.

scenes.tts: Their shared receptor subunit, g p one thirty, activates J A K kinases.
scenes.caption: Their shared receptor subunit, gp130, activates JAK kinases.
scenes.visual: Cytokine binds receptor with gp130; JAK kinases activate.
scenes.narration: Their shared receptor subunit, gp130, activates JAK kinases.

scenes.tts: J A K phosphorylates Stat three. Stat three switches on astrocyte genes, such as G F A P.
scenes.caption: JAK phosphorylates STAT3. STAT3 switches on astrocyte genes, such as GFAP.
scenes.visual: JAK phosphorylates STAT3; a STAT3 pair moves to the nucleus toward the GFAP gene.
scenes.narration: JAK phosphorylates STAT3. STAT3 switches on astrocyte genes, such as GFAP.

scenes.tts: Third, the progenitor must be able to read the signal. That is competence.
scenes.narration: Third, the progenitor must be able to read the signal. That is competence.

scenes.tts: Give C N T F to cortical progenitors early in neurogenesis. They have the receptor, and Stat three can be activated. What happens?
scenes.caption: Give CNTF to cortical progenitors early in neurogenesis. They have the receptor, and STAT3 can be activated. What happens?
scenes.visual: Early progenitor in a dish with CNTF dots; STAT3 lights up inside. Pause and predict.
scenes.narration: Give CNTF to cortical progenitors early in neurogenesis. They have the receptor, and STAT3 can be activated. What happens?

scenes.tts: Few G F A P positive astrocytes appear. In these early cells, the Stat three site in the G F A P promoter is methylated.
scenes.caption: Few GFAP-positive astrocytes appear. In these early cells, the STAT3 site in the GFAP promoter is methylated.
scenes.visual: Zoom to the GFAP promoter: a methyl tag sits on the STAT3 site.
scenes.narration: Few GFAP-positive astrocytes appear. In these early cells, the STAT3 site in the GFAP promoter is methylated.

scenes.tts: A methyl group on that site keeps Stat three from binding there. Stat three is active, but the G F A P gene does not answer.
scenes.caption: A methyl group on that site keeps STAT3 from binding there. STAT3 is active, but the GFAP gene does not answer.
scenes.visual: Activated STAT3 bounces off the tagged site; the GFAP gene stays dark.
scenes.narration: A methyl group on that site keeps STAT3 from binding there. STAT3 is active, but the GFAP gene does not answer.

scenes.tts: Later, demethylation and other changes in the cell let the same cytokine switch on G F A P.
scenes.caption: Later, demethylation and other changes in the cell let the same cytokine switch on GFAP.
scenes.visual: The methyl tag lifts off; STAT3 binds; GFAP turns on.
scenes.narration: Later, demethylation and other changes in the cell let the same cytokine switch on GFAP.

scenes.tts: So gliogenesis is timed partly inside the cell, not only by when the signal shows up.
scenes.visual: Card: timed inside the cell, not only by the signal.
scenes.narration: So gliogenesis is timed partly inside the cell, not only by when the signal shows up.

scenes.tts: What unlocks it? Cells that have just committed to becoming neurons carry Notch ligands.
scenes.visual: A newly committed neuron shows Notch ligands on its surface beside a progenitor.
scenes.narration: What unlocks it? Cells that have just committed to becoming neurons carry Notch ligands.

scenes.tts: In mouse cortex, Notch signaling in neighbouring progenitors induces a transcription factor, N F I A.
scenes.caption: In mouse cortex, Notch signaling in neighbouring progenitors induces a transcription factor, NFIA.
scenes.visual: Notch signal into the progenitor; NFIA appears in its nucleus.
scenes.narration: In mouse cortex, Notch signaling in neighbouring progenitors induces a transcription factor, NFIA.

scenes.tts: N F I A helps remove the methyl groups. So Notch, which first held progenitors back, has a second job: competence.
scenes.caption: NFIA helps remove the methyl groups. So Notch, which first held progenitors back, has a second job: competence.
scenes.visual: NFIA at the GFAP promoter; methyl tags lift. Label: Notch job 2, competence.
scenes.narration: NFIA helps remove the methyl groups. So Notch, which first held progenitors back, has a second job: competence.

scenes.tts: So, on this cortical cytokine route, a progenitor makes astrocytes when it is still there, given the signal, and able to read it.
scenes.visual: Closing card: still there, given the signal, able to read it.
scenes.narration: So, on this cortical cytokine route, a progenitor makes astrocytes when it is still there, given the signal, and able to read it.
